body:
OBSERVED 2026-08-20 on 0453cc2f0, proven by running the real parser.

Found by sweeping for the shape after /security-review flagged a below-bar instance
of it in PR #1774. The instance it found is the LEAST severe of the three.

## The shape, identical at three sites

    try:
        parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(raw)
    except ValueError:
        return None
    ...
    return parsed.astimezone(timezone.utc)      # <-- OUTSIDE the try

astimezone() raises OverflowError, not ValueError, when the shifted value leaves
datetime.MINYEAR..MAXYEAR. It is outside the guard at every site.

    cps/services/annotation_sync/__init__.py:51   LIVE Kobo annotation PATCH   <-- terminal
    cps/kobo.py:1927                              LIVE Kobo sync / reading state
    cps/annotations.py:365                        KoboReader.sqlite import (new in PR #1774)

## Proven, running the real function

    parse_client_modified_utc('2026-08-20T10:00:00Z')        -> 2026-08-20 10:00:00
    parse_client_modified_utc('not-a-date')                  -> None          (handled)
    parse_client_modified_utc('9999-12-31T23:59:59-23:59')   -> OverflowError ESCAPES
    parse_client_modified_utc('0001-01-01T00:00:00+23:59')   -> OverflowError ESCAPES

## Why the live-PATCH site is data-loss, not DoS

The value is device-supplied: raw_client_time = payload.get("clientLastModifiedUtc", ...)
at annotation_sync/__init__.py:205.

The code at :207-215 is DELIBERATE about this exact hazard and its comment says so - a
rejected clock reading must NOT discard the user's edit; it logs and stores the annotation
without a timestamp. That protection works for a malformed string ('not-a-date' -> None).
OverflowError bypasses it entirely, because only ValueError is caught.

It then meets F-5c1146: cps/readingservices.py handle_annotations wraps the capture block
in `except Exception: log.exception(...)` and returns proxy_to_kobo_reading_services()
unconditionally. So the device is answered SUCCESS for an annotation that was never stored.

And the Kobo uploads a DELTA, so it never re-offers it, while checkforchanges containment
(correctly) keeps the book out of the Kobo-cloud download that could have healed it.

Net: one out-of-range timestamp = one highlight silently gone forever, reported as success.
That is the same terminal mechanism F-5c1146 describes, reached by a different door.

## Not merely theoretical

A Kobo with a wrong clock, a corrupted row, or a firmware writing an unusual offset produces
this without anyone crafting anything. The value needs no privilege - it is ordinary sync traffic.

## Fix direction

Catch (ValueError, OverflowError) at all three sites and return None, which every caller
already handles correctly. The live-PATCH caller's existing "store it without a client
timestamp rather than discarding the highlight" branch is exactly the right landing place -
the bug is only that it is never reached.

Do NOT fix this by broadening the except Exception in handle_annotations; that is F-5c1146's
defect, not its remedy.

resolution.note: Fixed across #1776 (the two LIVE sites: annotation_sync parse_client_modified_utc and kobo.py parse_kobo_timestamp) and #1774 (the import site, cps/annotations.py). All three now keep parse, tz-validation and UTC conversion inside one guard catching (ValueError, OverflowError). The behaviour that matters is not 'returns None' -- an out-of-range clock now lands in the same branch a malformed one already did, so the highlight is STORED without a timestamp rather than destroyed. Live-PATCH storage property proven by a test that drives the real capture orchestration, red before the fix. NOTE: this widened F-4bb29a's reachability by one input class, recorded on that finding.

title: A device-supplied timestamp can silently destroy a highlight: OverflowError escapes every ISO clock parser
